title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
This page sets up notation for the second class of expressions in Euler's two-dimensional calculus of variations. There z = z(x,y) is a surface, and z is later embedded in a one-parameter family z(x,y,t).

Step 1. Euler continues the notation started on p.46.
- First derivatives: p = z_x, p' = z_y.
- Second derivatives: q = z_xx, q' = z_xy, q'' = z_yy.
- Third derivatives: r = z_xxx, r' = z_xxy, r'' = z_xyy, r''' = z_yyy.
- He records the compatibility relations r = q_x, r' = q_y = q'_x, r'' = q'_y = q''_x, r''' = q''_y. These rest on the tacitly assumed symmetry of mixed partials.
- Fourth derivatives: s = z_xxxx, s' = z_xxxy, s'' = z_xxyy, s''' = z_xyyy, s'''' = z_yyyy, 'and so on as far as one likes'. The k-th order block has k+1 symbols, indexed by the number of y-differentiations.

Step 2 (§21). An expression V of the second class is any function of x, y, z, p, p', q, q', q'', r, ... (a Lagrangian density depending on jets of z). He writes its total differential:
dV = L dx + M dy + N dz + P dp + P' dp' + Q dq + Q' dq' + Q'' dq'' + R dr + ... + R''' dr'''.
Here the capital letters are the partial derivatives of V with respect to each jet variable. The reader is asked to memorise this form.

Step 3 (§22). The variation is the increment produced by the new parameter t introduced into z. As for the first class, one sets dx = dy = 0 and dz = dt (dz/dt). The jet differentials are to be treated the same way. On the next page this gives dp = dt z_xt etc., hence the first variation
V_t = N z_t + P z_xt + P' z_yt + Q z_xxt + ...
This prepares the treatment of double integrals (the third class) and the Euler–Lagrange equation for functionals ∬ V dx dy.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The equality of mixed partials (e.g. q_y = q'_x) is used tacitly, which is standard for Euler. There is a minor typographical omission on the next page: dp' = dt(...) lacks the factor dt in the second equality. That slip is not on this page.

ideas.what: Systematic indexed notation for all partial derivatives of z(x,y) up to order 4 and beyond, with prime-index counting the y-differentiations
ideas.modern_name: jet coordinates / multi-index notation for partial derivatives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler for (dz/dx) partial notation; later Monge's p,q,r,s,t; jets formalised by Ehresmann (20th c.)
ideas.where_published: E420 itself; similar notation in Euler's Institutiones calculi integralis vol. III (E385) on PDEs

ideas.what: Compatibility relations among successive derivative symbols (symmetry of mixed partials)
ideas.modern_name: Schwarz/Clairaut theorem; contact (compatibility) relations in jet space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1734/1740 E44) and Clairaut; rigorous proof Schwarz 1873
ideas.where_published: E44 'De infinitis curvis eiusdem generis'; E420

ideas.what: Total differential of a function of jet variables, with coefficients L, M, N, P, Q, R as its partials
ideas.modern_name: differential of a Lagrangian on the jet bundle

ideas.what: Variation as the derivative with respect to an auxiliary family parameter t, with dx = dy = 0
ideas.modern_name: first variation as the Gateaux derivative along a one-parameter family of surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Elementa calculi variationum E296, 1766/1764) after Lagrange's δ-method

deep.surprise_reason: Purely notational set-up page of a well-known paper on the multivariable calculus of variations. Everything here is standard and documented in Euler's work and in histories of the calculus of variations.
transcription_corrections: Transcription matches the image closely. The fifth fourth-order symbol is printed s'''' (four primes), as transcribed. In the image the dV formula prints P' dp' (with 'dp'' slightly blurred as 'dp'') and places 'etc.' to the right of the second-to-fourth rows. No substantive corrections are needed.
